title: Ente Bhoomi & ILIMS
subtitle: How Kerala stitched together 30 million land parcels into a single, citizen-readable digital land information system.

citizen.summary: Getting a copy of your land record used to mean a day's wages lost, a visit to the village office, and a stack of photocopies. With Ente Bhoomi, it now takes ten minutes from your phone — and shows you everything: ownership, encumbrances, mutations, and the map.
story: For decades, every family transaction — a sale, a partition, a loan — depended on a thin paper record kept in a thick register at the village office. Disputes, errors and middlemen thrived in the gap between the citizen and that register.

Ente Bhoomi ("My Land") brings that register to your hand. It is built on top of ILIMS — the Integrated Land Information Management System — which links survey, revenue and registration data so the same parcel cannot be sold twice or mutated quietly.
changes: Land records are downloadable as authenticated digital certificates from your phone or any common service centre.
Survey maps now match revenue records — fewer disputes, faster mutations, less litigation.
Encumbrance information is visible upfront, protecting buyers from hidden liabilities.
Senior citizens, women, and tribal households can access records without depending on intermediaries.

overview: Kerala's land records existed in three parallel silos: the Survey Department's plot maps, the Revenue Department's ownership ledgers, and the Registration Department's transactions. Each was authoritative on its own, but together they often disagreed — and the citizen paid the price for that disagreement.

Ente Bhoomi is the citizen-facing front-end. ILIMS is the deeper plumbing: a unified geospatial database that reconciles survey, revenue and registration data into a single source of truth keyed on a unique survey number.

The initiative pairs a resurvey using drones and DGPS in selected blocks with a phased onboarding of legacy data — so the system grows in accuracy without waiting for a full statewide resurvey to finish.

challenges.title: Three departments, three truths
challenges.description: Survey, Revenue and Registration each maintained their own version of every parcel. Reconciliation rules had to be co-designed without making any department a "loser".

challenges.title: Legacy paper records, decades of accretion
challenges.description: Most ledgers were hand-written, many were torn, some were lost. A tiered digitisation strategy was needed — image first, key data second, full attributes third.

challenges.title: Public anxiety about errors
challenges.description: Citizens feared that going digital would lock in mistakes. A 30-day public objection window for every digitised parcel became non-negotiable.

challenges.title: Capacity of village officers
challenges.description: The system depends on the village officer cadre being comfortable with maps, mutations, and the new portal. Sustained training and on-call helplines were essential.

actions: Constituted a State Land Information Authority with cross-departmental membership — empowered to resolve reconciliation disputes.
Adopted a phased resurvey using drones, DGPS and ground control points, starting with high-litigation taluks.
Built ILIMS as an open-standards platform — APIs for banks, courts, and other departments to consume.
Launched Ente Bhoomi as the citizen-facing portal and app, in Malayalam first, English second.
Mandated a 30-day public objection window for every digitised parcel, with grievance redressal at the taluk level.
Linked Ente Bhoomi outputs to common service centres (Akshaya) for citizens without smartphones.
technology: PostGIS-backed geospatial database with parcel-level versioning
Drone-based aerial survey integrated with DGPS ground control
Open APIs for inter-departmental and bank/court integrations
Aadhaar-based eKYC and DigiLocker for authenticated downloads
Mobile-first Progressive Web App in Malayalam and English
Audit logs and tamper-evident certificate signing
outcomes: Over 30 million parcels mapped to ILIMS, with phased citizen-facing access.
Average wait time for ownership certificates fell from days to minutes in onboarded villages.
Mutation pendency dropped sharply — and is now publicly tracked at the taluk level.
Banks can verify encumbrances digitally, accelerating loan processing for citizens.
Estimated citizen time savings: equivalent to ₹420 crore annually in productive hours.

processFlow.title: 1. Block selection
processFlow.description: Pick high-litigation, low-coverage blocks for the first phase — early wins earn trust.

processFlow.title: 2. Aerial resurvey
processFlow.description: Drone + DGPS sweep generates a fresh, geo-referenced parcel map.

processFlow.title: 3. Reconciliation
processFlow.description: Survey, revenue and registration records cross-validated against the new map.

processFlow.title: 4. Public objection window
processFlow.description: Every parcel posted publicly for 30 days; objections heard at taluk level.

processFlow.title: 5. Citizen onboarding
processFlow.description: Ente Bhoomi portal goes live for the block; village officers trained and stationed.

processFlow.title: 6. Continuous mutation
processFlow.description: All new transactions flow through ILIMS, keeping the source of truth current.

replicationToolkit: Inter-departmental governance MoU template (Survey / Revenue / Registration)
Drone resurvey RFP boilerplate and quality specifications
30-day objection window SOP and citizen notice template
ILIMS API documentation and reference integrations

timeline.title: Governance MoU signed
timeline.description: Survey, Revenue and Registration departments co-sign reconciliation rules and form the State Land Information Authority.

timeline.title: Pilot resurvey begins
timeline.description: Drone-based resurvey starts in two high-litigation blocks; reconciliation rules tested in the field.

timeline.title: ILIMS goes live
timeline.description: Unified geospatial database operational; first inter-departmental APIs published.

timeline.title: Ente Bhoomi portal launched
timeline.description: Citizen-facing portal and mobile app go live in Malayalam and English.

timeline.title: 30M parcels milestone
timeline.description: Phased onboarding crosses 30 million parcels; certificate downloads average under 10 minutes.
